dominant_remains: command_graph_transition_gap is 81.5% across 243 intervals against 98 command buffers, roughly 2.5 gaps per command buffer. Submission and wait topology, not expert math and not the readbacks alone, is still where the recoverable time is.
method: ascension_qwen30_complete_native_runtime --mode forward-token --trace-dispatch, host_stage_intervals aggregated by bucket
note: Serial encoder groups were separately measured to have no end-to-end effect (0.34% across 3 trials each).
resizes_mechanism_m1: The router bucket is exactly the 48 host route-id readbacks, at ~1367 us each and 14.1% of the traced token. Mechanism M1 - device-indexed expert argument buffers to remove those readbacks - was estimated at 200-400 ms against the older 726 ms baseline. Measured against the current token that direct cost is ~65.6 ms, i.e. about 14%, not 200-400 ms. M1 remains worth doing and may additionally collapse some of the transition gap the readback waits force, but it is not by itself a path to the 100 rung.
